fields.h1: Build an Anonymous Feedback Form That Keeps Names Out
fields.hero_description: Build an anonymous feedback form with no name fields, results held for small groups, and comments saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Stores, and What It Never Asks
fields.features_subheading: An anonymous feedback form is only as private as what it stores. Emergent builds the fields and the table from one prompt.
fields.feature_1:
No field that asks who wrote it

Emergent builds the form without name, email, or employee ID fields, and with no sign-in. The response table has no columns for them either. No record ties a comment to a person.
fields.feature_2:
One question per screen on a phone

The form can show one question per screen, which suits a link opened from a QR code at the time clock. A rating, a topic, and one open comment fit in three taps and a short note.
fields.feature_3:
New comments in Slack or email

Each new comment can post to a private Slack channel or arrive by email for the person who acts on it. The alert carries the comment and its rating, and never a name or an email.
fields.feature_4:
Every comment in a database you own

Responses save as rows in a database you own, with a column for each question and the date. Filter one quarter by topic, or count how often the same complaint shows up again.
fields.feature_5:
No cap on how many people answer

Open the form to every team at once. Emergent sets no response caps. A busy week of comments never closes the form early or holds new answers back behind a monthly limit.
fields.feature_6:
The source code in your GitHub

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. An engineer can read exactly which fields the app stores, which helps when staff ask whether it is anonymous at all.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Places Unsigned Feedback Gets Used
fields.tab_content_1:
After the manager replies, the cook reads it by code

Copperpot Diner runs 3 locations and one staff suggestion form, opened from a QR code by each time clock. The form has no name or email field. Each submission gets a case code, such as MAPLE-3814. When general manager Delia Marsh posts a reply, the cook who wrote in enters that code to read it.
fields.tab_content_2:
Before a fifth answer, no manager sees a report

Twice a year, Brightfold Software asks every team to rate its manager. A report opens only after 5 direct reports have answered, because one comment from a tiny team is easy to trace. Tomas Achebe leads 7 people and has 4 answers. His report stays closed. The other 11 managers already see theirs.
fields.tab_content_3:
By Friday's close, 29 of 38 students answered

Dr. Nadia Brennan asks her Biology 140 class for anonymous feedback at midterm. The form saves the date of each answer but not the time. Without the time, a comment can't be matched to whoever left the lecture hall last. Results open when the form closes on Friday. Quiz pacing comes up most, in 11 comments.
fields.tab_content_4:
All 24 questions reach Marcus in one email by topic

Pinegrove Freight holds an all-hands every month on a Monday, and drivers send questions ahead through an anonymous form. On Sunday, the day before, the app emails CEO Marcus Odell all 24 questions grouped by topic. He starts with the new shift schedule, which leads with 7 questions.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Anonymous Feedback Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create an anonymous feedback form that stores no names, then build and test it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Drop every field that names a person
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set a minimum group for results
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down who will answer, how many of them there are, and the one decision the feedback should inform. A team of 6 needs different rules than a company of 400, and a single clear purpose keeps the form short.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Remove name, email, employee ID, and sign-in. Then check the fields that remain: a department plus a job title plus a start year can point to one person on a small team. Keep only the fields you will act on.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose a minimum number of answers before any report opens, such as 5. Apply it to every slice of the results, including a filter by department or by shift, and not only to the total count.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put the questions, the minimum group, and the columns the table should keep in one prompt. Emergent builds the form and the results view behind it, and you change any part of it by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Connect Slack or email for alerts and choose who receives them. Send each comment to the person who can act on it, and keep the channel private when comments may mention a shift or a manager by name.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide how people will hear back. Give each submission a case code, post replies in a shared channel, or answer the top themes at a team meeting. Tell people in the form's intro which of these you will use.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit a test answer from a phone, then open the response table. Check that no column holds a name or an exact time you did not plan for, and that results stay closed below your minimum.
fields.hero_prompt: Build an anonymous feedback form that saves every response to a database I own.

faq_plan.q: What is an anonymous feedback form?
faq_plan.a: An anonymous feedback form collects ratings and comments without recording who sent them. It asks for no name, email, or sign-in, and it leaves out any detail that could point to one person, such as an exact time on a small team.

faq_plan.q: How can I create an anonymous feedback form?
faq_plan.ref: How can I create an anonymous feedback form?

prov.original: How can I create an anonymous feedback form?

faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI form builder in one prompt: the questions, the fields to leave out, and how many answers must arrive before results open. Emergent builds the form and its database table, and you adjust either one by prompting. Send yourself a test answer before you share the link.

faq_plan.q: Should an anonymous employee survey ask for department or job title?
faq_plan.a: Ask for department only when every department will have at least 5 people answering, and skip job title wherever one title belongs to one person. Each extra detail makes a small group smaller. Emergent can build that minimum into the results view from your prompt, applied to every department filter.

faq_plan.q: What questions belong in an anonymous feedback form template?
faq_plan.a: Start with three questions: a rating on a 1 to 5 scale, a topic picker, and one open comment box. Add a question about what should change first if you want action items. Leave out name, email, employee ID, and start date, which belong in an employee information form kept apart from feedback.

faq_plan.q: Can I make a free anonymous feedback form with no limit on responses?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent's free tier covers building and publishing, and the forms Emergent builds have no response caps. Comments save to a database you own. If a developer later needs to audit the app, full code export to your GitHub repository is on paid plans.

faq_plan.q: What details can reveal who filled out an anonymous feedback form?
faq_plan.a: A sign-in or email, an IP address, an exact timestamp, or answers that fit one person, such as department plus tenure on a team of 4, can each point to the author. Check the defaults of any tool you use. SurveyMonkey's help center says Web Links record the IP addresses of respondents by default. It adds that turning on anonymous responses only applies to new responses.

faq_plan.q: How do I run an anonymous feedback form for a small group, like one training class?
faq_plan.a: Wait for a minimum count and report only totals. With a class of 8, open results after at least 5 have answered, and show ratings as a group average instead of one row per person. For a training feedback form after a single session, close it a day later, then share only the summary with the trainer.

faq_plan.q: How do I reply to someone who used an anonymous feedback form?
faq_plan.a: Reply in public when many people raised the same issue, or through a private code when one person did. A public answer at a team meeting shows that comments get read. The code lets one sender read a reply meant only for them. Emergent can build the code lookup into the same app, with each reply saved next to its comment.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep one person from sending an anonymous feedback form many times?
faq_plan.a: Hand out single-use codes instead of asking for names. Each person gets one code. The app marks a code as used when an answer arrives and saves the answer in a separate table with no link back to the code. Every code counts once, and no one can see which code wrote which comment.

faq_plan.q: How is an anonymous feedback form different from a performance review?
faq_plan.a: A performance review is signed, tied to one employee's record, and discussed with that person. Anonymous feedback has no author and is read as a pattern across many answers. Keep the two apart: use an employee evaluation form for reviews, and never copy anonymous comments into one person's file.

og.headline: Build an anonymous feedback form that keeps names out

plan.angle: The top 10 are form and survey builder templates (Typeform, Jotform, SurveyMonkey, SurveyHero, LimeSurvey, BlockSurvey, Formaloo) plus a Reddit thread from an academic hunting for a tool. They hand over a question list and a share link. The questions people ask next are all one worry: can the answer be traced back. This page answers with mechanics a builder controls: which fields and columns the form never has, a minimum number of answers before a report opens, a date with no time, and a reply that reaches the sender through a code, shown in four settings searchers have: a restaurant staff suggestion box, upward feedback on managers, midterm course feedback and questions for a company all-hands.

Dr. Nadia Brennan runs anonymous midterm feedback for Biology 140, the form saves the date of each answer but not the time, and when it closes on Friday 29 of 38 students have answered, with quiz pacing raised in 11 comments.

Pinegrove Freight collects anonymous questions before its monthly all-hands, and the day before, the app emails CEO Marcus Odell all 24 questions grouped by topic, 7 of them about the new shift schedule.
